Your team projects 69.0 points with Haaland captained. That hinges entirely on last season's data—scoring rates, starting frequency, and squad strength—so it doesn't yet account for summer moves, managerial changes, or shifts in playing time. Haaland carries meaningful upside (25% chance of 10+) but also real downside risk (8% chance of 2 or fewer), and he sits only 0.3 clear of Salah, your next option.

You're heavy on Arsenal and Manchester City, with three and two players respectively. That concentration amplifies both ceiling and floor. Your bench is thin: Mykolenko at 3.1 is the best of it, and the full four players project just 10.7 combined, so injuries to your starters would hurt.

No move clears its cost this week. You hold your transfer and start as built.

Your team projects 69.0 points with the armband on Haaland. That rests entirely on last season's data — scoring rates, starting frequency, and the strength each club showed then. Nothing here accounts for summer transfers, managerial changes, or shifts in squad status, so treat all projections as provisional until the first ball is kicked.

Hold. No transfer clears the points it would cost. Your bench is weak — Mykolenko at 3.1 is your best option if anyone doesn't play — but swapping anyone out demands a gain of at least 4 points to break even on the cost, and nothing you can afford does that. Your armband choice is tight: Haaland is 0.3 clear of Salah, but carries real downside risk (8% projected chance of 2 or fewer points) against Salah's steadier profile.

You have three Arsenal players in the eleven and two each from Liverpool and Manchester City. That concentration is intentional — it reflects how they performed last season — but it means your fortunes are tethered to how those three clubs start.

Gameweek 1 is opaque. Watch for team news before the deadline and be ready to move if anyone unexpected loses his place.

Your starting eleven projects to 60.8 points, or 69.0 with the armband on Haaland. That captain choice is marginal—only 0.3 points clear of Salah—but it holds: Haaland has a 25% chance of double digits against an 8% risk of scoring 2 or fewer. Salah is the natural alternative if you have second thoughts before the deadline.

You have three Arsenal players and two each from Liverpool and Manchester City. That's meaningful exposure to three of last season's strongest sides, but it also means your fortunes are tied to theirs. Your bench is thin; Mykolenko at 3.1 is the only backup worth mentioning.

No transfer improves the team after costs. Hold your free transfer.

Bear in mind that every projection here is built on last season alone. Summer moves, management changes and shifts in squad status are not yet accounted for. If you have credible news that a player's minutes or role have shifted materially, that would be the only reason to act.
